mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 5.0% in a sustained manner, it signals monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust economic expansion across supply and demand sectors, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in INDPRO and HOUST (both rising month-over-month) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained rise in core CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals persistent inflation that forces the Fed to maintain high rates, suppressing equity returns and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, CPIAUCSL above 2.5% y/y fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that boosts wages and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a monetary tightening cycle causing economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in FEDFUNDS and UNRATE fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In supply shock regimes, INDPRO below 100 fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.
